get.seeds: Seeds. Plant them in a hole.
get.bucket: A bucket. Fill it at the water.
get.knife: A mushroom knife. The brush cleans.

intro.speaker: npc
intro.text: Leave the sword. You won’t need it.

intro.speaker: npc
intro.text: You fought the dark. You won.

intro.speaker: npc
intro.text: Help the people here. Then the garden opens.

guide.speaker: npc
guide.text: Hollis, west. Iris, by the beds. Bram and Vega, north.

gate.speaker: npc
gate.text: Go to the fire in the middle.

after.speaker: npc
after.text: You found it. A place to sit.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Four neighbours need a hand.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Hollis, west. Iris, by the beds. Bram and Vega, north.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I study the fungi of this valley.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A mushroom is only the fruit. The fungus lives underground, as threads.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Six kinds grow here. Find them all. Take my knife.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Cut, don't pull. Brush, don't wash.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: All six. You know the forest floor now.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Keep them. Just never eat the red one.

puffball.speaker: npc
puffball.text: East, past the water: a white ball with no cap.

inkCap.speaker: npc
inkCap.text: North-east, by the pond: tall and white, shaggy like a wig.

morel.speaker: npc
morel.text: South, by the rocks: a cap like a honeycomb.

chanterelle.speaker: npc
chanterelle.text: Far north, under the pines: a golden funnel.

flyAgaric.speaker: npc
flyAgaric.text: The north-west corner: red, with white spots. Look. Don't eat.

porcini.speaker: npc
porcini.text: Far south, by the west edge: a brown bun on a fat stem.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Everything I paint is grey.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Here: seeds and a bucket. Plant them below me, water from the pond.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Green. Real green.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My woodpile’s empty. My hands shake.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take my axe. Four sticks from the dry trees?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Warm nights ahead.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Thank you, friend.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I want a cairn here, under the clearest sky.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take this pickaxe. Bring me one iron bar.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Iron. A place to come back to.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Thank you.

ore.speaker: npc
ore.text: Some rocks east of here hold ore. Break one.

furnace.speaker: npc
furnace.text: Ore needs a furnace. Build one at the bench.

charcoal.speaker: npc
charcoal.text: Set the furnace down. Two sticks make charcoal.

iron.speaker: npc
iron.text: Hammer the hot lump. Three blows.

cut.title: Cut
cut.aimKeys: Z when the blade is between the marks
cut.aimTouch: Tap when the blade is between the marks
cut.sawTouch: Swipe side to side to saw
cut.tooHigh: Too high. Cut close to the ground.
cut.tooHighVolva: Too high. Keep the cup at the base.
cut.tooDeep: Too deep. That tears the mycelium.
cut.mycelium: Those white threads are the fungus itself: the mycelium. Left in the soil, it fruits again.

clean.title: Clean
clean.why: Brush, don't wash: mushrooms soak up water.

puffball.cut: Cut under the ball, at the base.
puffball.clean: Brush off the soil and loose spines.
notes: No cap, no gills: the spores ripen inside the ball.
Its tiny cone-shaped spines rub off, leaving a net of scars.
Old ones turn brown and open a pore on top. A raindrop puffs out a cloud of spores.
Edible only while pure white inside. Cut it in half: a young amanita shows the outline of a cap.

inkCap.cut: Cut low on the slim stem. It's hollow.
inkCap.clean: Be quick: once picked, it turns to ink within hours.
notes: A tall white cap, shaggy with scales. Its other name: lawyer's wig.
As it ripens it digests itself from the rim, dripping black ink full of spores.
Grows in lawns and by roads, feeding on buried dead wood and roots.
It can even trap and digest tiny worms in the soil.
Edible only young and white, cooked the same day.

morel.cut: Cut at the base. The whole thing is hollow.
morel.clean: Grit hides in the pits. Brush each one.
notes: A honeycomb cap of pits and ridges, hollow from tip to base.
An ascomycete: its spores form in tiny sacs lining the pits, not on gills.
Morels come up in spring. Some kinds burst out after forest fires.
Poisonous raw. Edible only well cooked.
False morels are not hollow: they're stuffed with cottony tissue.

chanterelle.cut: Cut at the base, just above the moss.
chanterelle.clean: Dirt hides in the ridges. Brush them out.
notes: Egg-yolk yellow, shaped like a funnel with a wavy rim.
No true gills: blunt, forked ridges run down the stem.
Smells faintly of apricots.
It lives joined to tree roots, trading minerals for sugar. That's why no one can farm it.
Look-alike: the jack-o'-lantern has sharp true gills and grows in clusters on wood. Poisonous.

flyAgaric.cut: Cut below the soil line. The cup at the base, the volva, is how amanitas are told apart.
flyAgaric.clean: Brush gently: the white warts rub off.
notes: The white warts are scraps of a veil that wrapped the young mushroom like an egg.
White gills, a skirt-like ring on the stem, a swollen cup at the base.
It lives joined to birch and pine roots. That partnership is called mycorrhiza.
Its name comes from an old trick: crumbled in milk, it kills flies.
Poisonous. Never eat it.

porcini.cut: Cut at the base of the thick stem.
porcini.clean: Brush the cap. White pores underneath mean it's young.
notes: A brown, bun-like cap on a fat, club-shaped stem.
No gills: underneath is a sponge of tiny pores that drop the spores.
A fine white net covers the top of the stem.
It partners with pine, spruce and birch roots.
Edible and prized. Old pores turn yellow-green and soft.

opened.text: A gate opens in the middle of the valley.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The mushroom turns golden.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sword stays in the road.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nowhere to be. At last.
